Substantive operative text not available from this page alone. |

---

The regulation provides the following exemption categories, confirmed by the table of contents:

**Part 2 exemptions (tenant request regime):**
- Regulation 15: Consent exemption.
- Regulation 16: Devaluation exemption.

**Part 3 exemptions (prohibition on letting sub-standard property):**
- Regulation 31: Consent exemption.
- Regulation 32: Devaluation exemption.
- Regulation 33: Temporary exemption in certain circumstances.

*Source: The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015, table of contents. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2015/9780111128350/contents

*Specific conditions, evidence requirements, and duration for each exemption not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass* — the full enacted text of regulations 15, 16, 31, 32, and 33 is required.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any exemption is available to the workspace in respect of a specific property requires both the full enacted text and counsel review against the workspace's specific circumstances.

---

**MONITORING — re-check window: Q4 2025**

The UK government has consulted on raising the MEES minimum EPC band for non-domestic properties and has signalled further reform of domestic MEES thresholds. *Specific consultation outcome dates and any enacted amending instrument details are not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass* — the source block does not carry this information. The New Sources Identified section below flags the enacted instrument and DESNZ consultation pages as priority retrieval targets.

*Analytical inference:* Given the political and legislative trajectory toward higher energy efficiency standards for rented property in England and Wales, workspaces holding long-term commercial leases should monitor for amending instruments that raise the minimum EPC band threshold, which would affect both landlord compliance costs and the workspace's leverage in lease negotiations.

---

The table of contents confirms the following substantive requirement categories. Section-level text is not available in the source block; this section states the structural obligations as confirmed by the table of contents and flags where full text is required for operative detail.

**Part 2 — Tenant rights to energy efficiency improvements:**

The regulation establishes a framework under which a tenant may request consent to "relevant energy efficiency improvements" (regulation 6). The table of contents confirms:
- Regulation 8: Procedure for tenant's request for consent.
- Regulation 9: Circumstances in which a tenant's request may not be made.
- Regulation 10: Landlord's duty not to unreasonably refuse a tenant's request.
- Regulation 11: Superior landlord's duty not to unreasonably refuse a tenant's request.
- Regulation 12: Landlord's initial and full response to tenant's request.
- Regulation 13: Counter proposal process.
- Regulation 14: Effect of an improvement notice.

*Source: The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015, table of contents. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2015/9780111128350/contents

*Specific operative text of regulations 8–14 not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass* — the full enacted instrument is required to state the precise procedural requirements, timelines, and conditions.

**Part 3 — Prohibition on letting sub-standard property:**

- Regulation 23: Prohibition on letting of sub-standard domestic PR property.
- Regulation 27: Prohibition on letting of sub-standard non-domestic PR property.
- Regulation 24 / 28: Relevant energy efficiency improvements (domestic / non-domestic).
- Regulation 25 / 29: Relevant energy efficiency improvements undertaken.
- Regulation 26 / 30: Sub-standard property let in breach of the Regulations.

*Source: The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015, table of contents. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2015/9780111128350/contents

*Specific operative threshold (EPC band), applicable dates, and conditions for the prohibition not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass* — the full enacted instrument is required.

**Penalty provisions (penalty summary — required slot):**

- Regulation 38: Penalty notices.
- Regulation 39: Publication penalty.
- Regulation 40: Breaches in relation to domestic PR property.
- Regulation 41: Breaches in relation to non-domestic PR property.
- Regulation 42: Reviews, waiving and modification of penalties.

*Source: The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015, table of contents. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2015/9780111128350/contents

*Specific penalty amounts for domestic and non-domestic breaches not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass* — the full enacted instrument (regulations 40 and 41) is required to state the penalty figures. The structure of separate provisions for domestic (regulation 40) and non-domestic (regulation 41) breaches confirms that penalty levels differ by property type.

**PRS Exemptions Register (Part 3, Chapter 5):**

- Regulation 36: PRS Exemptions Register — landlords claiming an exemption must register specified information on the PRS Exemptions Register.
- The Schedule to the Regulations sets out the information to be registered.

*Source: The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015, table of contents and Schedule heading. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2015/9780111128350/contents

---

**What it is:**

The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015 establish a framework—commonly referred to as the Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards (MEES)—governing energy efficiency in privately rented property in England and Wales. The regulation covers both domestic and non-domestic private rented property.

The table of contents confirms the regulation is structured in three Parts:
- Part 1: Citation, commencement, general interpretation, service of documents, duty to review.
- Part 2: Tenant rights to request consent to relevant energy efficiency improvements, including landlord duties not to unreasonably refuse such requests, First-tier Tribunal applications, and exemptions.
- Part 3: Prohibition on letting sub-standard property, enforcement, penalties, and registration on the PRS Exemptions Register.

*Source: The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015, table of contents, legislation.gov.uk. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2015/9780111128350/contents

**Jurisdictional scope (required slot):**

The title of the instrument confirms its jurisdictional scope: England and Wales. *Source: "The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015," legislation.gov.uk. https://legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2015/9780111128350/contents

**Effective date (required slot):**

The source block is a draft instrument page. The legislation.gov.uk notice states: "This draft has been replaced by a new draft, The Energy Efficiency (Private Rented Property) (England and Wales) Regulations 2015 ISBN 978-0-11-113243-2." The effective date of the replacement enacted instrument is not carried in the available source block. *Specific effective date not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass — the source block is the superseded draft table of contents page only; the enacted instrument (ISBN 978-0-11-113243-2) must be retrieved for the confirmed commencement date.*

**Primary compliance deadline (required slot):**

The source block does not carry substantive deadline text. *Specific primary deadline not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass — the full enacted text is required.*

**Why it may apply to the workspace:**

*Analytical inference:* Freight forwarding operations routinely occupy warehousing, office premises, and logistics hubs in England and Wales under commercial leases. If any such leases are structured as "non-domestic PR property" as defined in the regulation, the workspace—in its capacity as tenant—may benefit from Part 2 rights to request energy efficiency improvements. *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any specific premises occupied by the workspace fall within the regulation's definition of "domestic PR property" or "non-domestic PR property" (as set out in regulations 19 and 20 of Part 3, and regulation 5 of Part 2) is a legal determination that depends on the precise lease terms and property classification; counsel review is required before asserting that the regulation applies.

---

*Operational implication:* For workspaces that hold or may hold a landlord position over commercial premises in England and Wales, the following operational capability gaps are structurally implied by the regulation's design, pending retrieval of the full enacted text:

1. **EPC tracking**: The prohibition on letting sub-standard property turns on the EPC band of each property let. Workspaces that sub-let premises must have a system to record the current EPC band of each sub-let unit and track whether it meets or falls below the operative minimum band. *Specific minimum band threshold not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass.*

2. **Exemption registration capability**: If an exemption is claimed (consent exemption, devaluation exemption, or temporary exemption), the workspace must register the required information on the PRS Exemptions Register. *Specific registration fields and process not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass.*

3. **Tenant request handling process**: If the workspace is a tenant and wishes to request energy efficiency improvements from a landlord, it needs an internal process to invoke regulation 8 rights, track landlord response timescales (regulation 12), and escalate to the First-tier Tribunal (regulation 17) if the landlord unreasonably refuses.

4. **Lease portfolio audit**: Before any of the above applies, the workspace needs a one-time audit of all England-and-Wales commercial leases to identify which, if any, fall within the regulation's scope.

*Operational implication:* Given that the source block is the superseded draft, any system build or process design should be validated against the enacted instrument (ISBN 978-0-11-113243-2 / SI 2015/962) before implementation.

sections.md:
### 7.1 Basic Inspection of Terminals (BIT) Program

FACT: "Under the BIT program, the CHP selects terminals for inspection based on the available carrier performance data or the commodity transported. Carriers must maintain and make available for inspection vehicles and records at the terminal(s) inspected as required by the California Vehicle Code (CVC) §§34501 and 34501.12." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

FACT: The MCSU Golden Gate Division conducts "Truck Terminal Inspections for those subject to the Biennial Inspection of Terminals (BIT) Program." *Source: Motor Carrier Safety Unit (Golden Gate Division), California Highway Patrol, current. https://www.chp.ca.gov/find-an-office/golden-gate-division/motor-carrier-safety-unit/

FACT: The BIT program scope also includes: "Controlled Substances and Alcohol Testing Program Inspections." *Source: Motor Carrier Safety Unit (Golden Gate Division), California Highway Patrol, current. https://www.chp.ca.gov/find-an-office/golden-gate-division/motor-carrier-safety-unit/

FACT: Not all carriers are subject to BIT: "Not all motor carriers who require an MCP need to participate in the Basic Inspection of Terminals (BIT) program." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces that garage and maintain vehicles at California terminal locations and whose commodity profile (hazardous materials, high-value cargo) triggers CHP selection criteria are at elevated BIT inspection risk. Readiness documentation — vehicle maintenance records, CSAT records, driver logs — should be maintained at terminal level in current, accessible form.

**Gap from current operational baseline:** The workspace profile indicates road operations; whether terminal-level documentation is maintained in the format and location required for BIT compliance is a gap that requires internal assessment.

### 7.2 Terminal Manager's Compliance Checklist

FACT: CHP 800D (Terminal Manager's Compliance Checklist, Rev. 04-17) is a CHP-issued checklist for terminal managers. *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with California warehouse or depot operations that serve as vehicle garaging locations, the CHP 800D checklist defines the inspection readiness standard. Operations leads should conduct an internal audit against this checklist before any anticipated BIT cycle.

### 7.3 Intrastate Electronic Logging Devices

FACT: The CHP Commercial Vehicle Section lists "Intrastate Electronic Logging Devices" as a program under Commercial Vehicle Section programs and services. *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

*Specific intrastate ELD implementation timeline and vehicle scope not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass.* The CHP page identifies this as an active program but the source content does not include the regulatory text or applicability thresholds.

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces operating intrastate California commercial vehicle movements and relying on paper logs should treat the intrastate ELD program as a pending compliance obligation requiring investigation with the CHP Commercial Vehicle Section at (916) 843-3400.

### 7.4 Hazardous Materials Transportation Licence and Route Compliance

FACT: The application process for a California Hazardous Materials Transportation License is set out in CHP 361E (Application Instructions) and CHP 361M (Application for Hazardous Materials Transportation License). *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with cargo verticals that include any IATA/IMDG-classified dangerous goods moving on the road leg in California — including lithium batteries, aerosols in event production kits, or automotive fluids — a separate hazardous materials licence is required in addition to the MCP. The licence and route compliance obligations are separate compliance streams.

### 7.5 Fleet Inspection and Maintenance Station Licence

FACT: CHP 361D (How to Obtain a Fleet Owner Inspection and Maintenance Station License) and CHP 361N (Application for Fleet Owner Inspection and Maintenance Station License, Rev. 4-12) are available for workspaces seeking to conduct in-house vehicle inspections. *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces with larger California road fleets — particularly those managing event or production vehicles with bespoke maintenance schedules — may achieve operational efficiency by obtaining a Fleet Owner Inspection and Maintenance Station licence, enabling in-house CHP-compliant inspections rather than dependence on third-party stations.

---

### ACTION REQUIRED — CA Number and Motor Carrier Permit Status

FACT: "The CA# is issued exclusively by the California Highway Patrol (CHP) to identify motor carriers and is used as the MCP number." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

FACT: "New carriers must apply for an MCP before they begin operations." *Source: Motor Carrier Permits, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/

*Operational implication:* For any workspace entity that operates, owns, or leases commercial vehicles in California and does not yet hold an active CA number and Motor Carrier Permit, operations are non-compliant from day one. Verification of current permit status is an immediate action item.

**Action:** Confirm that every California-operating entity in the workspace's road fleet holds a valid CA# and active MCP. Cross-check against the CHP's own active permit lookup (linked from the CHP Commercial Vehicle Section page).

---

### ACTION REQUIRED — Controlled Substances and Alcohol Testing Program (CSAT)

FACT: "CVC, Section 34520 requires both intrastate and interstate motor carriers to comply with the federal regulations." Applicable federal regulations cited include "Part 40 - Procedures for Transportation Workplace Drug & Alcohol Testing Programs" and "Part 382 - Controlled Substances and Alcohol Use and Testing." *Source: Safety Requirements, Caltrans, current. https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/legal-truck-access/safety

FACT: "The employer of the driver is responsible for conducting a 'controlled substances and alcohol testing' (CSAT) program that includes pre-employment testing, post-accident testing, random testing, and reasonable suspicion testing." *Source: Safety Requirements, Caltrans, current. https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/legal-truck-access/safety

FACT: CSAT applies to "drivers operating vehicles which require a commercial driver's license (class A, class B, or a class C with a hazardous materials endorsement)." *Source: Safety Requirements, Caltrans, current. https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/legal-truck-access/safety

*Operational implication:* For workspaces employing or contracting CDL drivers — including those handling hazardous materials, high-value cargo in Class A combinations, or event production equipment in Class B vehicles — a documented CSAT program is a standing operational requirement, not a one-time registration. The CHP BIT (Basic Inspection of Terminals) inspection scope includes CSAT compliance checks (see Section 8).

**Action:** Review CSAT program documentation against CHP form CHP 800F (Controlled Substances and Alcohol Testing Compliance Checklist, Rev. 7-17) and CHP 800J ("What is CSAT?", Rev. 9-16).

---

### ACTION REQUIRED — Liability Insurance Thresholds

FACT: "Levels of liability insurance vary from $300,000 to $5,000,000 combined single-limit coverage, depending on the type of vehicles and the property transported." *Source: Motor Carrier Permits, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/

*Operational implication:* For workspaces moving high-value cargo verticals (fine art, luxury goods, live events production equipment, high-value automotive), the applicable insurance threshold is at the upper end of this range. The workspace should confirm that active MCP insurance filings reflect current cargo type and vehicle class. An insurance shortfall at the time of a BIT or terminal inspection is a permit compliance failure.

**Action:** Pull the current Certificate of Insurance (MC 65 M) on file with DMV and verify the declared coverage level against the cargo verticals actually being transported.

---

### COST ALERT — MCP Fee Penalties for Late or Missed Renewal

FACT: "California Revenue and Taxation Code (RTC) §7236 imposes new penalties for failure to pay MCP fees, when due, on permit terms with an effective date of January 1, 2016, and later. Penalties will increase and continue to accrue until all fees are paid." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

*Specific penalty rate schedule not available from primary sources as of this brief's most recent authoring pass.* The DMV references an MCP Fee and Penalty Chart but the chart content was not accessible in the source blocks provided.

**Action:** Download the current MCP Fee and Penalty Chart from DMV and calendar MCP renewal dates to avoid accruing penalties.

---

### Carriers Exempt from MCP

FACT: The following do not require an MCP: "Household goods and/or passenger carriers as defined in §5109 of the Public Utilities Code (PUC) (these vehicles operate under Public Utilities Commission authority)"; "Pickup trucks with a GVWR of less than 11,500 pounds, an unladen weight of less than 8,001 pounds, and equipped with a box-type bed not exceeding nine feet in length, when operated in a non-commercial manner"; and "Two-axle daily rental trucks with a GVWR of less than 26,001 pounds, when operated non-commercially." *Source: Motor Carrier Permits, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces that periodically use short-term rental trucks for small-volume California moves (e.g., last-mile delivery of event materials in a light rental vehicle operated non-commercially), the MCP exemption for two-axle rental trucks under 26,001 lbs GVWR may apply. *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether "non-commercial" operation covers moves where the workspace is performing a service for a fee-paying client, even if the vehicle itself is rented and not for hire, requires counsel review against CVC definitions.

### Seasonal MCP for Intrastate For-Hire Operations

FACT: "A Seasonal MCP, commonly referred to as a Seasonal Permit, can be issued to an intrastate motor carrier operating on a 'For-Hire' basis for a period of no less than six months, but no more than 11 months in a 12 month term." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

FACT: "A seasonal MCP cannot be issued to an Interstate motor carrier." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with California intrastate operations concentrated in event seasons (live events, film and TV production season), the seasonal MCP pathway may offer a structurally lower administrative burden than a full annual permit. This is an intrastate-only option.

---

### 5.1 California Identification (CA) Number

FACT: "The CA# is issued exclusively by the California Highway Patrol (CHP) to identify motor carriers." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

FACT: "CA# applicants must complete a Motor Carrier Profile (CHP 362) (PDF) and mail, fax, or deliver it in-person to their closest CHP Motor Carrier Safety Unit." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

FACT: Processing time stated on the Golden Gate MCSU page: "When applying for a CA number, allow for ten working days after the Unit receives the application to issue a number." *Source: Motor Carrier Safety Unit (Golden Gate Division), California Highway Patrol, current. https://www.chp.ca.gov/find-an-office/golden-gate-division/motor-carrier-safety-unit/

*Operational implication:* A ten-business-day lead time for CA# issuance means new California operations cannot begin on short notice without prior compliance setup. For workspaces deploying assets to California for one-off events (live events, film and TV production transport), this timeline needs to be built into mobilisation planning.

### 5.2 Motor Carrier Permit (MCP) — Scope of Required Carriers

FACT: The MCP is required for: "Any person or business entity that is paid to transport property in their motor vehicle regardless of vehicle size, type, or weight"; "any person or business entity operating a commercial vehicle with a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) of 10,001 pounds or more"; "Operators of any vehicle or a combination of vehicles transporting hazardous materials"; and "Operators of a combination of a motor truck and trailer, semitrailers, pole or pipe dollies, auxiliary dollies, and logging dollies, that exceeds 40 ft in length when coupled together." *Source: Motor Carrier Permits, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces operating event production vehicles, art transport trucks, or automotive transport combinations that meet any of the above thresholds are within MCP scope regardless of whether California operations are frequent or seasonal.

### 5.3 MCP Term, Renewal, and Interstate Distinction

FACT: "An MCP term is the 12-month period beginning on the first day of the month of the initial application and expiring on the last day of the 12th month." *Source: Motor Carrier Permits, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/

FACT: "Interstate motor carriers are issued a non-expiring MCP and are not required to pay renewal fees, including the CIF." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with cross-border US operations that already hold a USDOT number and are classified as interstate carriers, the MCP renewal obligation is different from purely intrastate operators. Confirming the interstate vs. intrastate classification with the CHP is a compliance baseline action.

### 5.4 Driver Hours of Service

FACT: "Most drivers of commercial vehicles are required to maintain a logbook to record their hours of service." *Source: Safety Requirements, Caltrans, current. https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/legal-truck-access/safety

FACT: "Maximum driver hours for intrastate commerce (within California) have not changed. For intrastate requirements, see CVC Section 34501.2, and/or the California Code of Regulations (select Title 13, Division 2, Chapter 6.5, Article 3, Section 1212 'Driver Hours of Service')." *Source: Safety Requirements, Caltrans, current. https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/legal-truck-access/safety

FACT: The CHP Commercial Vehicle Section page references "Intrastate Electronic Logging Devices" as a program under the Commercial Vehicle Section. *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

*Analytical inference:* California's intrastate ELD programme extends electronic logging requirements to drivers operating solely within California. Workspaces with California-only road operations that have not yet assessed their ELD compliance exposure for intrastate movements should treat this as a gap requiring immediate investigation. (See Section 7 — Operational System Requirements.)

### 5.5 Load Securement

FACT: "California complies with the load securement requirements in the Code of Federal Regulations, Title 49, Parts 393.100 to 393.136." Additionally, "Several of the California Code of Regulations regarding load securement are still current. Title 13, Division 2, Chapter 7: Article 1. Protection Against Shifting Cargo; Article 2. Liquids In Collapsible Containers." *Source: Safety Requirements, Caltrans, current. https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/legal-truck-access/safety

*Operational implication:* For workspaces transporting high-value cargo (fine art, luxury goods, live events equipment, high-value automotive), load securement compliance is both a regulatory obligation and a cargo damage liability exposure point. CFR Title 49, Parts 393.100–393.136 set federal minimums; California Title 13 state regulations apply in addition.

### 5.6 Safety Equipment

FACT: "Commercial vehicles operating in California are required to be equipped with: a fully charged fire extinguisher securely mounted in a conspicuous place or in a marked compartment (further requirements may apply based upon type of cargo). Three properly maintained red emergency reflectors." FACT: "All vehicle (mechanical) equipment, such as lights, windshields, reflectors, etc., must comply with the United States Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration standards." *Source: Safety Requirements, Caltrans, current. https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/legal-truck-access/safety

### 5.7 Hazardous Materials Transportation

FACT: CHP forms for hazardous materials operations include: CHP 361E (Hazardous Materials Transportation License — Application Instructions), CHP 361M (Application for Hazardous Materials Transportation License), CHP 800C (Vehicles Transporting Hazardous Materials), and CHP 516/516A (Hazardous Agricultural Materials Certificate). *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

FACT: CHP route guidance documents for hazardous materials include HPH 84.5 (Inhalation Hazard Shipments: Routes and Stopping Places, Rev. 2-23) and HPH 84.3 (Explosive Materials Shipments: Routes, Safe Stopping Places, and Safe Parking Places, Rev. 05-21), with the caveat: "Check CHP's Regulatory Actions for most updated route maps and/or stop list through recent rulemaking." *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces moving dangerous goods by road in California — including lithium batteries for event production or automotive shipments — need a separate hazardous materials transportation licence and must operate on CHP-approved routes. Route maps are subject to rulemaking updates; static copies of HPH 84.5 and HPH 84.3 may not reflect current approved routes.

---

The CHP Commercial Vehicle Section administers California's commercial vehicle safety and enforcement program. FACT: "the CHP has established a goal of preventing the loss of life, injuries, and property damage through an innovative commercial vehicle safety program. This program encompasses enforcement, education, and partnerships to minimize the disastrous results from collisions involving commercial vehicles." *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

FACT: "The large presence of commercial vehicles in this state results in approximately 30 million miles of travel every day." *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

The framework applies to the workspace because road transport is a core mode in the workspace's operational profile. Workspaces arranging or operating commercial vehicle movements in California — including drayage for air-freight ground legs, event logistics trucking, and high-value cargo road transfers — are within the scope of this program. *Analytical inference:* For workspaces with air-primary, road-secondary transport profiles, the road leg (drayage to and from airport, venue delivery, or warehouse transfer) is the primary point of CHP commercial vehicle compliance exposure.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, acting as freight forwarder arranging third-party carriage rather than operating vehicles directly, qualifies as a "motor carrier" subject to CHP permitting and inspection obligations under California Vehicle Code §34501 requires counsel review, as the answer turns on operational facts (who owns and operates the vehicles, who holds the CA#).

**Effective status:** This is an active, enforced state program. No sunset date is identified in the source material.

---

The California commercial vehicle compliance framework places obligations at the level of the motor carrier — the entity that owns, leases, or operates commercial vehicles. The workspace's position in this chain depends on operational structure:

**Scenario A — Workspace operates own commercial vehicles in California:**
*Analytical inference:* The workspace is the motor carrier of record and holds (or must hold) a CA# and MCP. All BIT, CSAT, vehicle inspection, and insurance obligations attach directly.

**Scenario B — Workspace arranges carriage by third-party California carriers:**
*Analytical inference:* The workspace's direct obligations are reduced, but due-diligence exposure remains — particularly for high-value and hazardous cargo verticals where shipper responsibilities under load securement and hazardous materials regulations may still apply.

**Scenario C — Workspace is a logistics intermediary that sometimes takes on motor carrier functions (e.g., leasing vehicles, employing drivers for specific moves):**
*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace's hybrid role creates motor carrier obligations under CVC §34501 and related sections, and which entity in a multi-party arrangement holds the compliance obligation, requires counsel review.

FACT: Section 34623(h) of the California Vehicle Code states "A motor carrier of property may not operate a commercial motor vehicle on any public highway in this state during any period its motor carrier of property permit is suspended pursuant to this division." *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

*Operational implication:* Suspension of a carrier partner's MCP during an active shipment would render continued road movement non-compliant. Workspaces should include permit status verification in carrier onboarding and spot-check protocols.

---

---

### CA Number Application

FACT: The CHP 362 (Motor Carrier Profile, Rev. 3-18, 5 pages) is the application form for a new or updated CA number. Applications can be submitted online or by PDF to the nearest Division office. *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

### USDOT Number

FACT: The CHP Commercial Vehicle Section page links to the FMCSA for USDOT number applications, updates, and data quality challenges. *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

### Unified Carrier Registration (UCR)

FACT: The CHP Commercial Vehicle Section page links to the UCR renewal portal. *Source: CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, California Highway Patrol, current. https://chp.ca.gov/programs-services/programs/commercial-vehicle-section.

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces with interstate operations, UCR registration is a parallel federal obligation that coordinates with but is distinct from the California MCP/CA# requirement. Both must be current for compliant cross-border operations involving California.

### Employer Pull Notice (EPN) Program

FACT: Carriers are required to "Get a valid Requester Code issued by the Employer Pull Notice (EPN) Program if you employ drivers with a Commercial Class A, Commercial Class B, or Class C driver license with a hazardous materials or any other applicable endorsement (required by California Vehicle Code (CVC) §15278)." *Source: Motor Carrier Permits, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/

*Operational implication:* The EPN requirement extends to any workspace employing CDL drivers with hazmat endorsements — a common profile for workspaces handling dangerous goods in any cargo vertical.

### Workers' Compensation Insurance

FACT: "All motor carriers are required to provide proof of compliance with California's Workers' Compensation laws." Acceptable proof includes a Certificate of Insurance (MC 65 M), a certificate from the State Compensation Insurance Fund, or a Certificate of Consent to Self-Insure. *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

FACT: "A motor carrier who employs only family members is required to provide workers' compensation insurance." *Source: Motor Carrier Permit FAQs, California DMV, current. https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/motor-carrier-services-mcs/motor-carrier-permits/motor-carrier-permits-mcp-faqs/

---

This document synthesises sourced information from the CHP Commercial Vehicle Section, the California DMV Motor Carrier Permit program, Caltrans safety requirements, and the CHP Golden Gate Division Motor Carrier Safety Unit (MCSU). It applies the California commercial vehicle safety and compliance framework to the workspace's operational profile as a freight forwarder and logistics intermediary operating commercial vehicles or arranging transport by road in California. It does not provide legal advice. Items requiring legal determination are labeled *Legal Confirmation Required:*. Every substantive claim is labeled FACT, ANALYSIS, or LEGAL per the claim-level provenance contract.

**Convention notes:**
- "The workspace" refers to the operator described in the workspace profile.
- All binding-verb sentences are either span-grounded FACTs with inline citations, labeled ANALYSIS/inferences, or routed to *Legal Confirmation Required:* callouts.
- The FMCSA California FY23 CVSP source was inaccessible (access denied); no claims are drawn from it.
- The Justia regulations source returned a bot-verification wall; no claims are drawn from it.

Golden Gate Division Motor Carrier Safety Unit Motor Carrier Safety Unit The Motor Carrier Safety Unit's primary function is to conduct safety inspections of commercial vehicle operators within the nine Bay Area counties. Motor Carrier Permitting Active Motor Carriers Motor Carrier Permit FAQs Notification icon Read the MCP News Bulletin for important information regarding future renewals. Drivers who transport property, operate large commercial vehicles, transport hazardous materials, or operate vehicles requiring a commercial driver’s license need a motor carrier permit (MCP) as evidence they have registered their California Carrier Identification number (CA#) with DMV. Drivers Who Need an MCP The following types of drivers and/or vehicle operation require an MCP: Any person or business entity that is paid to transport property in their motor vehicle regardless of vehicle size, type, or weight. Entities that transport property for compensation are deemed a ‘for-hire’ motor carrier. If you are a courier service and your vehicle is a motorcycle, you are required to have an MCP. Generally, any person or business entity operating a commercial vehicle with a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) of 10,001 pounds or more. This includes commercial and private use. Entities operating vehicles hauling personal goods or property are deemed a ‘private’ motor carrier. Operators of any vehicle or a combination of vehicles transporting hazardous materials. Operators of a combination of a motor truck and trailer, semitrailers, pole or pipe dollies, auxiliary dollies, and logging dollies, that exceeds 40 ft in length when coupled together.* Operators of any motor vehicle or combination of motor vehicle and trailer for which the operation requires a commercial driver license.* *Operators pulling camp trailers, utility trailers, and trailer coaches do not need an MCP. Drivers Who Do Not Need an MCP The following types of drivers and/or vehicle operation do not require an MCP: Household goods and/or passenger carriers as defined in §5109 of the Public Utilities Code (PUC) (these vehicles operate under  Public Utilities Commission  authority). Household goods carriers transporting used office, store, and institutional furniture and fixtures when operated under a household goods carrier permit issued pursuant to §5137 of the PUC. Operators of: Pickup trucks with a GVWR of less than 11,500 pounds, an unladen weight of less than 8,001 pounds, and equipped with a box-type bed not exceeding nine feet in length, when operated in a non-commercial manner. Vehicles providing transportation for passengers and their baggage only. Two-axle daily rental trucks with a GVWR of less than 26,001 pounds, when operated non-commercially. Vehicles which are exempt from vehicle registration fees. Motor trucks or two-axle truck tractors with a GVWR of less than 26,001 pounds, when operated singly or when used to tow a camp or utility trailer, a trailer coach, a fifth-wheel travel trailer, or a trailer designed to transport a watercraft, and is never operated commercially. How to Apply for an MCP New carriers must apply for an MCP before they begin operations. You can apply online or by mail. To apply online: Complete and submit the online MCP application . To apply by mail: Get a CA# from the California Highway Patrol (CHP) (see the FAQs for more information). Complete an Application for Motor Carrier Permit (MC 706 M) (PDF) . Provide proof of insurance (see “Insurance Requirements” below). Provide proof of Workers’ Compensation insurance or signed exemption. Get a valid Requester Code issued by the Employer Pull Notice (EPN) Program if you employ drivers with a Commercial Class A, Commercial Class B, or Class C driver license with a hazardous materials or any other applicable endorsement (required by  California Vehicle Code (CVC) §15278). Pay applicable fees. Make a copy of your application for your records, then mail your application, documentation, and fees to: Department of Motor Vehicles Registration Operations Division PO Box 932370 – MS H875 Sacramento, CA 94232-3700 Overnight delivery: Department of Motor Vehicles Registration Operations Division 2415 1st Avenue – MS H875 Sacramento, CA 95818 MCP drop box: Department of Motor Vehicles Building West Lobby 2570 24th Street Sacramento, CA 95818 You cannot submit your application at a DMV office. An MCP term is the 12-month period beginning on the first day of the month of the initial application and expiring on the last day of the 12th month. The MCP will not be issued until all requirements are met. Fees Permit fees are based on the type of motor carrier operation (for-hire or private) and the number of power units in the motor carrier fleet. See the MCP Handbook (PDF) to find your fees. Insurance Requirements Levels of liability insurance vary from $300,000 to $5,000,000 combined single-limit coverage, depending on the type of vehicles and the property transported. Proof of insurance must be submitted on one of the following forms (CVC §34631,  California Code of Regulation (CCR) §220.06): Certificate of Insurance (MC 65 M) from your insurance provider. Certificate of Self Insurance (MC 131 M). To apply for a Certificate of Self Insurance, a motor carrier must meet the following requirements: The motor carrier fleet is comprised of 25 or more commercial vehicles registered in the motor carrier name. The required level of liability insurance does not exceed $750,000. There are no unsatisfied judgment(s) against the motor carrier name or the “doing business as” (DBA) or trade names resulting from property damages and/or bodily injury (including death) caused by a motor vehicle accident listed on the application. Self Insurance Forms Motor Carrier Application for Certificate of Self Insurance (MC 130 M) (PDF) . Assignment of Deposit Motor Carrier Permit Certificate of Self Insurance (MC 133 M) (PDF) . Request for Voluntary Termination of Motor Carrier Permit Certificate of Self Insurance – (MC 132 M) (PDF) . How to Renew an MCP You can renew an MCP when you: Have a valid permit on active status and are renewing the permit for the next term. Are renewing a permit that has been expired less than a year. Are renewing a permit with minimal changes. Are requesting a voluntary withdrawal of the permit, in lieu of the Request for Voluntary Withdrawal Motor Carrier Permit (MC 716 M) (PDF) form. To renew your permit online: Complete and submit the online MCP application . How to modify an MCP Complete and submit a Motor Carrier Permit Notice of Change (MC 152 M) (PDF) to: Make a name change. Make an address and/or phone number change. Add or delete a DBA name. If the business entity has changed in anyway, you must obtain a new CA# from the CHP and file a new MCP application. A Fictitious Business Name Statement is required when adding a DBA name. Mail the form to: Department of Motor Vehicles Registration Operations Division PO Box 932370 – MS H875 Sacramento, CA 94232-3700 Overnight delivery: Department of Motor Vehicles Registration Operations Division 2415 1st Avenue – MS H875 Sacramento, CA 95818 MCP drop box: Department of Motor Vehicles Building West Lobby 2570 24th Street Sacramento, CA 95818 How to withdraw an MCP If you wish to cease operations as a permitted motor carrier before you cancel/terminate liability insurance and/or before your permit expires, complete and submit a  Request for Voluntary Withdrawal Motor Carrier Permit (MC 716 M) (PDF) . You can also complete a voluntary withdrawal with a MCP Renewal Application (MC 134 M) (with certification). If you fail to submit a completed and signed MC 716 M or MC 134 M at the time of discontinuation of operations, you may incur delinquency fees upon your return to the program. Mail your completed form(s) to: Department of Motor Vehicles Registration Operations Division PO Box 932370 – MS H875 Sacramento, CA 94232-3700 Overnight delivery: Department of Motor Vehicles Registration Operations Division 2415 1st Avenue – MS H875 Sacramento, CA 95818 MCP drop box: Department of Motor Vehicles Building West Lobby 2570 24th Street Sacramento, CA 95818 Unified Carrier Registration (UCR) Pay UCR Online Letter to All Carriers Subject to UCR Act (PDF) Refunds To request a fee refund, complete and submit an Application for Refund (ADM 399) (PDF) after you complete your MC 716 M. A refund will only be issued when the vehicle will not be operated intrastate in California during the next term and the new permit term has not begun. If your application has no errors and does not need to be reviewed, you can expect your bank account to be charged in 2-3 business days after you submitted your MCP renewal application. However, if your renewal application requires further review, funds will be withdrawn later. Please allow 30 days before inquiring about your MCP. Will I get a receipt? Expand Accordion Plus Collapse Accordion Minus Yes, a receipt will be mailed once your submitted payment has been entered into our MCP system and your MCP has been issued. When will I receive my new MCP? Expand Accordion Plus Collapse Accordion Minus Please allow for 30 days to receive your renewed MCP via mail. After 30 days, if you do not receive your MCP, please contact the Motor Carrier Permit Unit at 916-657-8153. General FAQs May I apply for an MCP at my local DMV Field Office? Expand Accordion Plus Collapse Accordion Minus No. The single point of contact for all matters related to the MCP program is the Registration Operations Division located at DMV Headquarters in Sacramento, California. The MCP Operations Unit is not open to the public. However, there is a public drop box labeled “Motor Carrier Permit” at: Department of Motor Vehicles Building West Lobby 2570 24th Street Sacramento, CA 95818 For more information, contact MCP Operations . What is a Seasonal MCP? Expand Accordion Plus Collapse Accordion Minus A Seasonal MCP, commonly referred to as a Seasonal Permit, can be issued to an intrastate motor carrier operating on a “For-Hire” basis for a period of no less than six months, but no more than 11 months in a 12 month term. Seasonal carrier fees are based on the size of the fleet and are comprised of the Safety Fee plus one twelfth of the Uniform Business License Tax (UBLT) for each month the MCP is valid, along with the full Carrier Inspection Fee (CIF). Seasonal carriers will pay the CIF only once in their seasonal term. Extensions can be requested for a fee of $5 plus one-twelfth of the UBLT based on the fleet size per additional month of operation in the seasonal term. A seasonal MCP cannot be issued to an Interstate motor carrier. MCP Fee and Penalty Charts How do I obtain a Carrier Identification number (CA#)? Expand Accordion Plus Collapse Accordion Minus The CA# is issued exclusively by the California Highway Patrol (CHP) to identify motor carriers and is used as the MCP number. CA# applicants must complete a Motor Carrier Profile (CHP 362) (PDF) and mail, fax, or deliver it in-person to their closest CHP Motor Carrier Safety Unit. Not all motor carriers who require an MCP need to participate in the Basic Inspection of Terminals (BIT) program (see below). For more information, visit the CHP website or contact the closest Motor Carrier Safety Unit, the Commercial Records Unit, or Commercial Vehicle Section (see page three of the CHP 362 form). Do I need to provide proof of Workers' Compensation insurance? Expand Accordion Plus Collapse Accordion Minus Yes, all motor carriers are required to provide proof of compliance with California’s Workers’ Compensation laws. Submit one of the following or certify on the Application for Motor Carrier Permit (MC 706 M) that you are not subject to California workers’ compensation laws: A Certificate of Insurance (MC 65 M). A Certificate of Insurance electronically submitted by the State Compensation Insurance Fund (SCIF). A Certificate of Consent to Self-Insure issued by the by the director of the Department of Industrial Relations (DIR) of the Office of Self-Insurance Plans (OSIP). A signed exemption statement, stating that in your operations as a motor carrier you do not employ any person in any manner so as to become subject to the workers’ compensation laws of California. For additional information regarding Workers’ Compensation requirements and laws, go to Department of Industrial Relations or call them at 1-800-736-7401. If I only employ family members in my business, is Workers' Compensation insurance required? Expand Accordion Plus Collapse Accordion Minus Yes, a motor carrier who employs only family members is required to provide workers’ compensation insurance. All fees applicable to the type of motor carrier operation are due upon application for an MCP. California Revenue and Taxation Code (RTC) §7236 imposes new penalties for failure to pay MCP fees, when due, on permit terms with an effective date of January 1, 2016, and later. Penalties will increase and continue to accrue until all fees are paid. MCP Fee and Penalty Charts What is the Basic Inspection of Terminals (BIT) program? Expand Accordion Plus Collapse Accordion Minus Under the BIT program, the CHP selects terminals for inspection based on the available carrier performance data or the commodity transported. Carriers must maintain and make available for inspection vehicles and records at the terminal(s) inspected as required by the California Vehicle Code (CVC) §§34501 and 34501.12. sections.md:
## Iowa as a Through-State Corridor

A material volume of freight moving through Iowa originates outside the state: "a significant amount of freight originates outside of Iowa and moves through the state to destinations in other states." *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

*Operational implication:* For workspaces routing east–west or north–south intermodal freight across the Midwest, Iowa's highway and rail network functions as a transit corridor, not only an origin-destination market. This expands the strategic relevance of Iowa freight planning beyond Iowa-domiciled shippers.

## Federal Reauthorization Alignment

Recent Federal Transportation Reauthorization Acts have "placed increasing emphasis on the importance of the efficient movement of freight and encourage States to consider freight movements in their overall planning processes." *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

*Analytical inference:* Federal freight emphasis increases the probability that Iowa DOT investment priorities — surfaced in the Five-Year Highway Program and State Freight Plan — align with federally designated freight network projects, which in turn affects access to FHWA freight formula funding and the BUILD/INFRA grant programs. Workspaces operating on corridors that intersect federally designated freight routes may benefit from infrastructure investment cycles driven by this alignment.

## Multi-State Rail Connections: CPKC and Union Pacific

CPKC Railroad and Union Pacific Railroad both hold FAC membership. *Source: Freight Advisory Council Member List, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council *Analytical inference:* CPKC's Trans-America corridor and Union Pacific's midwest network mean that Iowa rail connects to Gulf, Pacific, and Canadian border gateways — a cross-regional implication for workspaces sourcing or delivering into Iowa agricultural and industrial supply chains. Specific interchange and intermodal ramp locations are not confirmed from the source blocks.

## Commodity Dependency: Agriculture and Energy

The FAC membership includes representation from Iowa Farm Bureau, Landus Cooperative, Sukup Manufacturing, NEW Cooperative, and Agribusiness Association of Iowa, alongside energy logistics operator Travero (the FAC Chair's employer). *Source: Freight Advisory Council Member List, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council *Analytical inference:* Iowa's freight demand is structurally weighted toward agricultural commodities (grain, fertilizer, equipment) and energy (ethanol, wind energy components). Workspaces servicing distribution, logistics, or industrial supply chains in Iowa will encounter seasonal freight demand peaks driven by harvest cycles and planting seasons, and year-round demand driven by energy infrastructure buildout.

---

## Iowa DOT's Planning Framework as a Procurement Signal

The State Freight Plan is "one of a variety of additional plans and tools the department utilizes to ultimately inform the development of the Five-Year Program." *Source: Iowa State Freight Plan, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2022. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/transportation-plans/freight-plan *Analytical inference:* The Five-Year Highway Program is the capital deployment instrument. Workspaces or their clients whose freight corridors align with Five-Year Program investment priorities gain access to improved infrastructure ahead of corridors that are not prioritized. Monitoring the Five-Year Program update cycle creates an early signal for route-level infrastructure changes.

## FAC as a Stakeholder Access Point

The FAC was "created in 2012 as a forum to assist with understanding the complexities associated with freight movements through education, discussion, and review." Members represent agriculture, energy, distribution, logistics, and multimodal transportation, as well as local and state government agencies, and "meet on a quarterly basis to address critical topics cooperatively identified by the FAC Chair and Iowa DOT staff." *Source: Freight Advisory Council, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council

*Analytical inference:* Participation in or direct engagement with FAC-affiliated operators (Amazon DSM5, Ruan Transportation, Decker Truck Lines, Iowa 80 Group, Perishable Distributors of Iowa) gives workspaces insight into freight mobility priorities before they are formalized in plans and investment programs. The FAC's quarterly meeting cadence produces publicly available meeting materials — a low-cost intelligence source.

## Named Operators Active in Iowa

The FAC membership provides the following named operator-level participants (all citations: *Source: Freight Advisory Council Member List, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council):

- **Ruan Transportation** — Marty Wadle, Chief Commercial Officer, FAC Vice-Chair. Iowa-based transportation and logistics operator.
- **Decker Truck Lines** — Bob Elkins, Chief Operating Officer. Iowa-based truckload carrier.
- **Iowa 80 Group** — Delia Moon-Meier, Senior Vice President. Operator of truck stop and logistics services on I-80.
- **Perishable Distributors of Iowa** — Joe McConnell, Vice President of Transportation. Temperature-controlled distribution operator.
- **Amazon DSM5** — Doug Martin, Assistant General Manager. Amazon distribution center in Des Moines metro.
- **Travero** — Jillian Walsh, Senior Business Development Manager, FAC Chair. Multi-modal logistics operator (formerly Cargill's transportation business).
- **Ten D, Inc. / Companies/Merchants Distribution Service** — Greg Dickinson, President. Distribution services.
- **Des Moines Industrial** — Gabe Claypool, President.
- **John Deere Des Moines Works** — Matt Leyser, Manager of Factory Order Fulfillment. Heavy equipment manufacturing and outbound logistics.

*Analytical inference:* These named operators represent the active freight market in Iowa across trucking, temperature-controlled distribution, heavy equipment, agricultural supply chain, and e-commerce fulfillment. Workspaces positioning for Iowa freight business will compete or partner within this operator set. No sourced data on market share, contract terms, or competitive positioning beyond membership affiliation is available from the source blocks.

## Multi-Modal Access: Highway, Rail, Waterway, Air

Iowa's transportation system is explicitly described as comprising airports, highways, pipelines, railroads, and waterways, all of which "play a major role in supporting the state's economy." *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

**Road:** Highway is the primary freight mode. The Iowa DOT operates an oversize and overweight permit system, IFTA (International Fuel Tax Agreement) compliance, and IRP (International Registration Plan) registration — all active and accessible to motor carriers. *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

**Rail:** The 2025 Iowa State Rail Plan is the active governing document. *Analytical inference:* The plan's explicit focus on "promoting access to rail transportation, helping to improve the freight railroad transportation system" signals that rail remains a feasible secondary mode for bulk and industrial cargo, though capacity and interchange details require carrier-level confirmation. *Source: Iowa State Rail Plan, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2025. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/transportation-plans/rail-plan

Rail operators with active representation on the Iowa Freight Advisory Council (FAC) include CPKC Railroad (Ryan Nonnemaker, Director of U.S. Government Affairs), Union Pacific Railroad (Kelli O'Brien, Director of Public Affairs for IA, MN, and WI), and Iowa Interstate Railroad (Joe Parsons, Chief Operating Officer). *Source: Freight Advisory Council Member List, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council

**Waterway:** Waterway access is confirmed as part of Iowa's transportation system. The Port of Blencoe is referenced through FAC membership (Frank Huseman, Operations Manager, NEW Cooperative/Port of Blencoe), and the Upper Mississippi River inland waterway was the subject of an alternative financing study in 2019. *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers maintains representation on the FAC through both the Rock Island District (Tom Heinold) and the Omaha District (Lt. Col. Charles McWilliams), covering both the Mississippi and Missouri River corridors. *Source: Freight Advisory Council Member List, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces moving bulk agricultural or energy commodities, barge access via the Upper Mississippi and Missouri River systems represents a cost-competitive alternative to road and rail for high-volume, non-time-sensitive moves. Feasibility is corridor- and commodity-specific; rate availability requires direct carrier inquiry.

**Air:** Aviation is listed as a component of Iowa's transportation system and the Iowa DOT administers an Aviation Plan and airport improvement programs. *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight Specific air cargo capacity figures and airport freight throughput data are not available from the source blocks provided.

*Specific air cargo throughput and capacity figures not available from primary sources at the time of this authoring pass.*

## Oversize and Overweight Permitting

The Iowa DOT operates an active oversize and overweight permit system with online application capability. Permit types and requirements are published. *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight *Analytical inference:* For workspaces moving heavy industrial equipment, large-format event infrastructure, or oversized cargo (consistent with live events, film and TV, or high-value automotive verticals), the Iowa permit system is an established pathway — but dimensional limits and corridor restrictions require permit-specific confirmation.

---

## What the Workspace Can Credibly Say

1. **Iowa's multi-modal system is structurally intact and state-prioritized.** The Iowa DOT operates highway, rail, waterway, and aviation freight planning as an integrated system, guided by a federally approved State Freight Plan and a 30-year state transportation plan (Iowa in Motion 2050). *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

2. **Federal freight funding alignment is active.** The State Freight Plan has been formally approved by FHWA. *Source: Iowa State Freight Plan, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2022. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/transportation-plans/freight-plan *Analytical inference:* FHWA approval signals eligibility for freight formula funding allocations — relevant to clients evaluating infrastructure-dependent supply chains in Iowa.

3. **Iowa is a transit corridor, not just a destination.** "A significant amount of freight originates outside of Iowa and moves through the state to destinations in other states." *Source: Iowa DOT Freight Overview, Iowa Department of Transportation, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight This is a credible talking point for clients evaluating Iowa as a consolidation or transload location.

4. **The 2026 freight plan update is underway.** The Iowa DOT has published a draft State Freight Plan for public comment. *Source: Iowa DOT Invites Comments on the Draft State Freight Plan, Iowa Department of Transportation, February 24, 2026. https://iowadot.gov/news/2026-02-24/iowa-dot-invites-comments-draft-state-freight-plan Workspaces can credibly represent awareness of this update cycle to clients as evidence of active market intelligence.

## Claims to Avoid

- Do not claim specific Iowa freight rates, lane costs, or modal cost comparisons without a sourced figure — none are available in the source pool.
- Do not characterize Iowa's infrastructure as "excellent" or "deficient" without reference to a specific plan section; the State Freight Plan's performance reporting (Chapter 2) addresses this but the full text was not provided.
- Do not represent FAC membership as implying an endorsement of any specific operator's service quality. Membership is an advisory role, not a procurement credential.

## Questions to Pose to Iowa-Based Clients

- Which commodity verticals does your Iowa freight move support — agriculture, energy, or industrial? (Modal and seasonal implications differ materially.)
- Are your Iowa volumes origin-destination or through-freight? (Corridor planning implications differ.)
- Does your operation use rail interchange at any Iowa point? (2025 Rail Plan may affect interchange priorities.)
- Are any of your Iowa shipments oversize or overweight? (Permit system is active and online; lead time should be confirmed.)

---

Freight Resources Plans & Programs Studies Contacts The term freight can be defined as “the transport of goods from one place to another”. The State of Iowa has a large and diverse economy that demands the efficient transport of freight.  There is a growing need to move freight safely, securely, and efficiently. Iowa’s transportation system of airports, highways, pipelines, railroads, and waterways play a major role in supporting the state’s economy. An efficient multi-modal system for moving freight to, from and within the state is critical to Iowa’s economic competitiveness and directly affects our quality of life. Iowa’s transportation system is also important to regional and national freight movements as a significant amount of freight originates outside of Iowa and moves though the state to destinations in other states.  Recent Federal Transportation Reauthorization Acts have placed increasing emphasis on the importance of the efficient movement of freight and encourage States to consider fright movements in their overall planning processes.  This website helps provide an overview of Iowa’s freight transportation system – helping to identify what it looks like, what some of the key issues are, to identify planning initiatives being undertaken by the department to address these issues, and to provide direction in the planning and investment of freight transportation needs in the State of Iowa. The plan was formally approved on August 18, 2022. The primary purpose of the State Freight Plan is to document the immediate and long-range freight planning activities and investments in the state. More specifically, it will provide guidance on how to address issues, adapt to emerging trends, and invest strategically in the freight system to grow a stronger economy, strengthen the nation’s competitive advantage, and enhance the quality of life for Iowans. Developed in coordination with the Iowa Freight Advisory Council, the State Freight Plan serves as a platform for connecting Iowa’s freight-related initiatives and a tool for informed decision-making aimed at addressing the ongoing challenges of today’s freight system and supply chains. This plan is the second in the current series of freight plans that are now federally required to be updated every four years. The 2022 State Freight Plan is an updated and streamlined version of the original with several notable enhancements that will impact the freight transportation system. Relationship to the State Transportation Plan The State Freight Plan is developed to support the State Transportation Plan. More specifically, the following freight-specific items will align with the four Iowa DOT system objectives (safety, sustainability, flow, and accessibility) documented in the state transportation plan. Freight goals Implementation strategies Improvements/investments Performance measures Each of Iowa’s freight-related initiatives plays a role in a collaborative planning and programming process. The State Freight Plan is one of a variety of additional plans and tools the department utilizes to ultimately inform the development of the Five-Year Program. These include the State Transportation Plan, more specialized plans, system evaluations, and project-level evaluation tools. Back to top Read the Plan Plan Overview Archived Iowa in Motion 2050 Full Document (Web version; reduced file size) Archived Iowa in Motion 2050 Full Document (Print Version) Archived Chapter 1: Looking Ahead Archived Introduction and overview of the plan and planning process Chapter 2: Understanding Iowa Archived Demographic and economic trends Chapter 3: System Overview Archived Overview of each mode and passenger and freight trends Chapter 4: Objectives and Considerations Archived Iowa’s transportation vision, key objectives, and factors shaping future planning and development Chapter 5: Needs, Risks, and Strategies Archived Analysis of needs, risks, strategies by mode, highway risk matrix, and Iowa DOT’s rightsizing policy Chapter 6: Paying Our Way Archived Projected costs, revenues by mode, and strategies to address funding shortfalls Chapter 7: Making It Happen Archived Programming future investments and ongoing performance monitoring Appendices Archived Federal requirements, public input, mobility analysis, plan strategies, and revenue mechanisms Back to top About the Plan List items for State Transportation Plan Background Iowa’s state transportation plan was adopted in May 2022. In 2024, an administrative modification was made to the plan to incorporate the following three implementation activities that had occurred since plan adoption: the Carbon Reduction Strategy, Resilience Improvement Plan, and Transportation 4.0: Innovative strategies for the transportation revolution. The plan looks out to 2050 and provides the long-range vision, policies, and decision-making framework that will guide investments in Iowa’s transportation system over the coming years. Iowa is required to have a long-range transportation plan by both federal and state code. The plan covers all modes of transportation in the state, for both people and goods. The plan is updated every five years because Iowa’s transportation system is ever-changing. Proactively planning for the future of the system is critical to ensuring people and goods can get where they need to go in a safe manner. The needs for the system are continually evolving due to changes in demographics, land use, travel patterns, technology, and available funding. The plan establishes the vision and objectives for the state’s multimodal transportation system, identifies existing and emerging needs, risks, and challenges, and recommends strategies to achieve the vision for the transportation system. This plan is the third in the current series of long-range plans. In 2012, a policy level plan was adopted. In 2017, the plan was expanded to identify primary investment areas, categorize future needs across modes, and provide strategies to achieve the system vision. The 2022 plan builds on these past plans by making enhancements that include: Additional focus on emerging planning considerations Establishment of system objectives Expanded analysis of highway system needs and risks Updated strategies to implement the plan Development of Iowa DOT’s rightsizing policy Development Materials Presentations to the Iowa Transportation Commission during the plan development process are posted below. This group was created in 2012 as a forum to assist with understanding the complexities associated with freight movements through education, discussion, and review. Members representing the agriculture, energy, distribution, logistics, and multimodal transportation industries, as well as local and state government agencies, meet on a quarterly basis to address critical topics cooperatively identified by the FAC Chair and Iowa DOT staff. This guidance allows the Iowa DOT to more effectively guide public investment in the freight transportation system with the ultimate goal of enhancing the competitiveness of Iowa’s business and industry. Iowa State Freight Plan - Executive Summary - FAST Act Doc.pdf 2.06 MB .pdf About List items for Freight Advisory Council Mission To guide the Iowa DOT in fostering a safe, efficient, and convenient multimodal freight transportation system to enhance the competitiveness of Iowa’s business and industry. Goal Through education, discussion and review, the Freight Advisory Council will assist and advise the Iowa DOT on freight mobility policies, programs, and investments. Values Open discussion and respect for a variety of interests and opinion.s Commitment to regular participation and other assigned responsibilities. Collaborative decision-making that provides the best end result for Iowa’s freight transportation system and future economic vitality. Responsibilities Responsibilities may include but are not limited to: Serve as an advisory body to Iowa DOT staff involved in freight mobility activities. Identify obstacles, challenges, and inefficiencies in the current freight transportation system. Proactively identify emerging trends that may impact freight mobility. Provide educational opportunities to stakeholders. Assist in the development of the Iowa DOT’s State Freight Plan, including providing stakeholder input, reviewing draft content, and offering suggestions for improvement. Review and comment on modal plans and the state long-range transportation plan as they relate to freight mobility. Review and comment on proposals for freight policies, programs, and investments. Consult with interested constituents as appropriate. Suggest potential planning initiatives or research topics. Advocate for freight mobility issues. Organization Meet on a quarterly basis. Meetings will be held at a central Iowa location; one meeting per year may be held at another location of the state. A chair and vice chair will be elected to serve a two-year term and the vice chair will assume the chair position at the end of the chair’s term. Term limits will not apply to general membership; however, if a member or designee is absent for three consecutive meetings, barring extenuating circumstances, their membership will be terminated. Agendas will be cooperatively developed by the chair and Iowa DOT staff. Meeting arrangements will be the responsibility of the Iowa DOT. Iowa DOT will provide other staff support, as needed.
